title: S Chand and Company Ltd - 540497 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: S Chand FY26 EBITDA hit Rs1,449m (18.1% margin) with net cash Rs1,048m; FY27 revenue growth guided at 10-15%, margin at 17-19%.
summary.overview: FY26 revenue came in at the guided Rs8,000m, with gross margin held near 68% despite a 6% GST hike on paper. EBITDA rose to Rs1,449m (18.1% margin, within the 18-20% guidance) and PAT grew 21% to Rs731m. Operating cash flow was Rs747m, below the ~Rs1,000m five-year average, because receivables (160 days) and inventory (232 days) rose. Management guided FY27 operating revenue growth of 10-15%, EBITDA margin of 17-19% (1pp below FY26), and OCF above Rs1,000m.

vs Rs1,401m and 223 days in Q4FY25

segments.name: Publishing (curriculum/school books)
segments.commentary: Growth was mainly volume-led with muted pricing; publishing margins improved as the mix shifted toward sourced content in digital, per management. Old and new syllabus books were adopted in FY26, and new series (Mylestone, My Zen, SmartK, Solid Steps) are in over 1,500 schools.

segments.name: Digital / AI dataset content licensing
segments.commentary: Revenue grew over 60% YoY in FY26, with management citing roughly Rs32 crore in FY25 and Rs40 crore targeted for FY27. Digital margins were lower than last year despite Rs10-11 crore of incremental revenue, which shows the margin dilution from sourced content (sourced share rose from about 20% to 70%).

segments.name: International (CPD Singapore)
segments.commentary: Acquired January 2026; supplementary books for Singapore/IGCSE/IB curricula. Last-year revenue was about USD0.5m (Rs5-6 crore), with sales only in Singapore and Malaysia. Management expects roughly Rs5-7 crore of capex over 2-3 years and a 1-2 year build-up in India.

guidance_outlook: FY27 operating revenue growth of 10-15%, mainly volume-driven.
FY27 EBITDA margin band of 17-19%, below FY26 because of paper, logistics, packaging and fuel cost inflation; management expects a 6-8% price increase.
Operating cash flow above Rs1,000m in FY27; receivables and inventory expected to normalise in 1H FY27.
Content licensing revenue target above Rs400m in FY27; management says this is a pipeline view and may change.
FY27 year-end net cash of about Rs130-135m after roughly Rs20 crore capex; buyback under consideration once the war-related uncertainty settles.
Full NCF (new syllabus) adoption expected across K-12 over FY27-28.
capex_capacity: Rs20 crore capex this year is mainly for a new state-of-the-art printing plant near Delhi with more space and digital printing (POD) machines.
About 80-85% of printing is in-house and 15-20% outsourced; the new plant is aimed at in-sourcing and improving working capital.
Management did not give a margin contribution from the new plant in the first one or two years.
International business capex of Rs5-7 crore expected over 2-3 years; team of 10-15 people.
Raw material (paper) inventory was about Rs29 crore at year-end, equal to under a month in peak season and about 3 months off-peak.
demand_pricing: Paper prices expected up 10-15% for FY27; supplier negotiations were not finalised at the time of the call.
Price increases are capped at about 6-8% because of customer pushback.
Around 40-60% of paper is imported, depending on the year; a stronger dollar and higher logistics costs are a factor.
Higher education has shrunk from about 20% of the business pre-COVID to about 8%, citing piracy and lower book purchases by students; school segment is up 20-25%.
Management estimates a 10-15% market share in private school publishing and a school retention rate above 70%.
AI licensing: about 30-40% of the content repository is licensed to date; about 100% of term-license renewals so far have been retained; pricing is varied and has seen a slight correction.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 10-15% growth guidance inclusive of any NCF upside, and how big can AI licensing become?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 10-15% is a sound guidance on a large base, with growth volume-driven. AI licensing targets Rs100 crore over time; it is a mix of one-time (about 30%) and term licences (about 70%). Management said it would not give margins due to client confidentiality, though in-house content is near 90% margin.

qa_highlights.question: Why is there no buyback despite a strong net cash position and low valuation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a buyback is under consideration and the Board will decide later. It is waiting for the war-related uncertainty to ease and for paper and consumables prices to settle. FY27 year-end net cash is expected at about Rs130-135m.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins return to 25%?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the company now prioritises cash conversion over margin. Operating cash flow was Rs800m-era levels of Rs38m in the past versus Rs75m this year, and the company wants working capital efficiency and not revenue growth that does not convert into cash.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Rs400m+ licensing revenue be from in-house or sourced content?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects roughly 60% in-house and 40% sourced, based on the current pipeline. The target is per SKU or title licensed, not per user.

qa_highlights.question: Why are the entities kept separate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said each acquired brand has its own sales team and school relationships, which lets the group capture more of each child's book bag. Consolidation would risk losing market share.

risks_watch: Working capital: receivables at 160 days and inventory at 232 days; management expects normalisation in 1H FY27, which needs to be checked in the Q1 numbers.
Margin pressure from paper, fuel and logistics inflation; the 17-19% band is below FY26's 18.1%, and FY27 price hikes are capped at 6-8%.
Dependence on AI licensing: revenue is lumpy, pricing is varied, and client budgets are the stated constraint; margin on sourced content is lower.
Middle East conflict is delaying collections from schools in the region.
Higher education decline (about 8% of the mix from about 20% pre-COVID).
Integration and returns from CPD Singapore; management said more clarity will come next year.
Buyback and dividend decisions remain open; the company is currently paying Rs4/share interim dividend.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the school-segment outlook, NCF and AI licensing, but cautious on near-term costs and cash. Management was evasive on AI licensing margins (citing NDAs), on the buyback timing, and on the link between pricing and the syllabus change.
key_quotes: We are proud to say that we continue to be net debt-free company at the end of FY26 through consistent efforts on working capital management.
At this point of time, whatever profits we are earning is coming to us in cash.
So far, it is, as I would say, 100% customer retention.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 operating revenue growth of 10-15% (midpoint 12.5%), mainly volume-driven, backed by school segment growth of 20-25%, a 6-8% price increase, and a Rs20 crore new printing plant near Delhi aimed at in-sourcing rather than new output; EBITDA margin guided down to 17-19% from 18.1%, and the brief gives no quarterly revenue or EBITDA growth figures.
